title: RAM<->VRAM KV Tiering Feasibility

hot_cold_policy_signals_section16.note: research-only listing, per Section 16 -- none implemented this phase (Section 7 scoped to manual/static placement only).
signals: token recency (position relative to current generation point)
sliding-attention-window membership (irrelevant for the two models tested this phase -- see sliding_window below)
layer usage / activation magnitude over recent decode steps
attention score magnitude (how much a given cached position is actually attended to)
context position (absolute distance from the start of the sequence)
host/GPU memory pressure (current free VRAM vs a budget, reusing the same real gpu_policy signals membrane-run already computes)

sliding_window_attention_section17.finding: both test models (SmolLM2-135M and SmolLM2-360M) use FULL attention, confirmed live from real model-load output: n_swa=0, is_swa_any=0, every individual layer reports is_swa=0.
sliding_window_attention_section17.implication: for these two models, 'old KV is cold' is at least not immediately falsified by attention semantics -- every position genuinely COULD be attended to by a later token, so demoting old KV to RAM never discards data the model structurally cannot use again. This would NOT hold for a genuinely SWA or hybrid-attention model (documented in llama.cpp's own hparams.swa_type/n_swa machinery, confirmed present in the pinned source -- see architecture.json) -- a future phase testing such a model would need to verify which layers/positions a sliding window actually excludes before assuming any KV is safely 'cold.' Not assumed universally true here, checked directly against the actual models used, per Section 17's explicit instruction.

final_report.architecture_classification: E. REQUIRES_LLAMA_CPP_CHANGE for the phase's actual target (KV placement decoupled from weight placement); a real, usable, coarser COPY_POSSIBLE-adjacent mechanism (combined weight+KV static offload) already exists with zero new code -- see architecture.json for the full nuance, not a single clean letter.
final_report.public_api_findings_headline: byte-level GPU<->host copy of a real, live, single KV cache tensor is proven safe via 100% public API (cb_eval + ggml_tensor::view_src + ggml_backend_tensor_get/set) -- new working infrastructure MEMBRANE did not have before this phase. Independently rebinding/freeing ONE layer's GPU buffer while siblings stay resident is NOT possible (shared-buffer allocation). KV cache buffer-type resolution is hard-coupled to the SAME per-layer device assignment used for model WEIGHTS (model.dev_layer(il)) -- there is no public way to place only the KV cache differently from its layer's weights.
final_report.whether_upstream_change_required: yes, for the phase's actual target capability (KV-only placement, weights staying GPU-resident, with controlled movement). The smallest identified fix is a new optional kv_dev_override callback in llama_kv_cache's constructor (third_party/llama.cpp/src/llama-kv-cache.cpp, ~lines 211-225), mirroring the shape of the already-existing, already-accepted kv_type_override patch. NOT written this phase, per Section 2.
final_report.tiering_granularity: per-layer chosen as the primary, proven unit (smallest granularity both cleanly supported by an existing public mechanism AND producing a real measured VRAM win); per-tensor proven reachable for live COPY only, not for independent VRAM release; whole-cache proven reachable via llama_state_seq_get/set_data for live serialize/restore, also without VRAM release.
final_report.copy_roundtrip_proof: real, live SmolLM2-135M context, ctx=2048: single K tensor (786432 bytes) copied GPU->host, GPU copy deliberately zeroed to prove same backing memory, restored, byte-for-byte identical (FNV-1a checksum match) to the pre-movement original, generation continued correctly for 4 more tokens. See roundtrip_correctness.json.
final_report.authoritative_placement_proof: real external nvidia-smi VRAM reduction confirmed for the coarse (weight+KV combined) --gpu-layers N mechanism at every tested context (SmolLM2-135M ctx 2048/8192/16384, SmolLM2-360M ctx 2048) -- NOT a shadow copy (GPU allocation genuinely smaller). Roughly HALF of the measured saving is weight VRAM, not KV VRAM specifically (memory_accounting.json) -- true KV-ONLY authoritative placement (weights staying GPU-resident) was not achieved, per the upstream-change finding above.
final_report.gpu_ram_byte_accounting: GPU_KV + RAM_KV == expected total KV bytes exactly, in every tested configuration (memory_accounting.json) -- e.g. 100270080 + 100270080 == 200540160 at SmolLM2-135M ctx=16384/Q8/tiered.
final_report.vram_reduction: tiering-alone (weight+KV combined) saved 114-199 MiB across ctx 2048/8192/16384 on SmolLM2-135M, 2.2x-3.7x more than Q8->Q5 precision compression alone at the same points, and the two effects combine additively. See vram_reduction.json.
final_report.second_model_result: SmolLM2-360M ctx=2048 reproduces the same pattern (322 MiB tiering-alone saving vs 13 MiB precision-alone), no fallback, correct exit codes. See second_model.json.
final_report.pressure_test: at ctx=186000 through ctx=205000 on the known GTX 1650 constrained region (SmolLM2-360M), tiered Q5 (16/32 GPU layers) succeeds cleanly where BOTH whole-cache adaptive AND whole-cache explicit Q5 already fail -- a genuine ~10-13% usable-context extension using an existing, already-shipped mechanism, with the true ceiling likely understated by the current (not-yet-tiering-aware) memory estimator. See pressure_test.json.
final_report.correctness: the round-trip's exact byte-level restoration (roundtrip_correctness.json) mathematically guarantees post-movement generation is token-identical to a no-movement reference, since the model's forward pass is a deterministic function of that exact KV state -- no quantization error introduced by movement itself, confirmed by construction.
final_report.copy_bandwidth_latency: 0.55-0.70ms / 786KB for a single layer (1.1-1.4 GB/s effective); scales to 34-75ms for all 30 layers (47 MB) at the same rate class; GPU->host (get) consistently slower and noisier than host->GPU (set); effective bandwidth far below PCIe theoretical because non-pinned host memory forces the SYNCHRONOUS backend path (see prefetch_feasibility.json). See copy_microbench.json.
final_report.decode_throughput_impact: single-layer targeted movement is cheap (under 3.5% stall even at ctx=16384). The deliberately worst-case scenario (ALL layers, synchronously, every 8 tokens) is expensive and gets WORSE at larger contexts: 7.5% stall at ctx=2048 but 47% stall and roughly halved generation throughput at ctx=16384. See decode_impact.json.
final_report.async_prefetch_feasibility: real async transfer infrastructure exists in the pinned Vulkan backend (dedicated transfer queue, event/fence primitives, already used internally by ggml_backend_sched) -- but requires Vulkan-PINNED host memory to activate; none of this phase's probes used pinned memory, so the measured bandwidth numbers are synchronous-path numbers, not a fair test of async's real potential. See prefetch_feasibility.json.
final_report.failure_behavior: invalid/out-of-range/negative layer selection and a missing model file all fail closed with clear, non-zero exit codes, no crash, no silent data loss, live-tested. Several failure modes (insufficient RAM/VRAM on promotion, mid-transfer copy failure, backend mismatch) were reasoned about but not live-tested, since no promotion/demotion runtime was built this phase (manual/static scope only). See failures.json.
final_report.tests: 15 new llama-free unit tests (test_tiering_placement_policy: partition validity, duplicate-ownership rejection, gap rejection, out-of-range/negative rejection, exact byte accounting, budget-limit checks, deterministic manual split matching the real llama.cpp trailing-layer convention, and a promotion/demotion state-machine with only 4 valid transitions) -- all pass, plus the graph-node-name and live-movement/decode-impact probes (real GPU integration tests, not unit tests, run manually this session).
final_report.sanitizers: llama-free Release + ASan/UBSan: 64/65 tests pass; the 1 failure (test_mem_guard) is a pre-existing, environment-sensitive test unrelated to this phase's changes (touches tools/membrane-kv-exact-sim, not modified here), reacting to this shared host's real low available memory -- same finding, same root cause, as Phase 11E's regression_sanitizers.json. llama-enabled CPU ASan/UBSan and the full Vulkan product regression matrix (native/q8/q5/adaptive/compare/gpu-bench/auto/guard) were NOT re-run in full this session for the same real host-memory-constraint reasons Phase 11E disclosed; the Vulkan paths this phase's OWN experiments exercise (q8, q5, adaptive, gpu-layers N) all ran repeatedly and cleanly with no_fallback_occurred=true and correct exit codes throughout Sections 9-11's real runs.
final_report.verifier: scripts/verify-results.py extended with new Phase 12A checks (provenance, partition/accounting arithmetic recomputed from raw data, VRAM claims cross-checked against the raw nvidia-smi numbers, pressure-test claims backed by the raw pass/fail exit codes, no unsupported product claims, no private paths, manifest completeness); mutation-tested.
limitations: true KV-only tiering (weights staying GPU-resident) was not achieved -- the demonstrated VRAM win is a combined weight+KV effect from the pre-existing --gpu-layers N mechanism, not a novel KV-specific capability (see memory_accounting.json)
async/pinned-memory transfer performance was not measured -- all copy/decode-impact numbers are synchronous-path numbers
no promotion (RAM->GPU on demand) mechanism was built or tested -- Section 7 scoped this phase to manual/static placement only

decode-impact scenarios reload the model fresh per scenario (for clean isolation), so absolute cross-scenario comparisons carry some model-load-variance noise -- the qualitative finding (worst-case scenario D is expensive, others are not) is robust to this, exact percentages less so
llama-enabled ASan/UBSan and the full product regression matrix were not re-run in full this session, for real, disclosed host-memory-constraint reasons
unresolved_issues: exact per-layer boundary of --gpu-layers N's trailing-layer split was not independently re-verified via debug logs against the real formula (i_gpu_start = n_layer+1-n_gpu_layers) for the specific models used -- only the AGGREGATE effect (VRAM delta, gpu_layers_selected) was directly measured

the product's own gpu_policy memory estimator does not yet account for tiered (partial-offload) KV placement correctly -- it still charges the FULL whole-cache KV total against the GPU budget regardless of --gpu-layers N, meaning the true tiering ceiling (pressure_test.json) is understated by the product's own conservative math; not fixed this phase (would touch tools/membrane-run/gpu_policy.c, a product file, out of this phase's research-only scope)

decision_gate_rationale: The phase's actual target capability -- authoritative KV cache placement across GPU VRAM and system RAM, independent of weight placement, with controlled movement -- requires a llama.cpp change (decoupling llama_kv_cache's per-layer buffer-type resolution from model.dev_layer(il), which currently also governs weight placement). This was identified precisely (file, function, smallest fix, upstreamability, maintenance risk -- architecture.json) and NOT written, per Section 2's explicit STOP instruction. This verdict is not a rejection of tiering as a direction: this phase also produced substantial, real, positive evidence (a working, public-API-only single-tensor live copy mechanism; genuine external VRAM reduction and a real usable-context extension on the actual constrained hardware from an already-EXISTING, already-shipped mechanism) that should inform whatever comes next, but that existing mechanism moves weights and KV together, which is a different, coarser capability than what this phase set out to prove feasible.
next_step_recommendation: Design and, in a future phase, propose the smallest llama.cpp patch (the kv_dev_override callback in llama-kv-cache.cpp, mirroring kv_type_override's existing shape and precedent) that decouples KV cache buffer-type resolution from weight buffer-type resolution -- this is the single blocking change standing between this phase's proven building blocks (safe live single-tensor copy, real VRAM accounting) and true KV-only RAM<->VRAM tiering. Do NOT execute it in this phase.
